prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit / ui-mockup. Make a LOCALIZED refinement to the RIGHT CANVAS BACKGROUND ONLY in ONE Ascend Studio screen.
Image 1 is the exact edit target. Image 2 is color/material inspiration only for the faint cyan, lavender, pink, mint and apricot palette. Match image 1's 1672 x 941 landscape framing. Current date 2026-10-09; add no dates or labels.

User request: the right canvas decoration must not be a solid colored object or surface. It should be a FLOWING CONNECTIVE PATTERN at the bottom of the canvas, a subtle atmosphere that occupies no layout space and dissolves into the base background.

LOCK EVERYTHING EXCEPT THE RIGHT CANVAS'S DECORATIVE BACKGROUND:
Preserve the left project archive-plane background exactly at its current low strength; preserve the middle conversation's faint reciprocal curves exactly. Preserve logo/breadcrumb, three columns, compact navigation/task rows, headings, all exact content, text, neutral selected rows, conversation without avatars and without an AI bubble, right-aligned user bubble, code/evidence cards, canvas dot grid, object positions, toolbar, minimap, zoom and hand controls. Keep text crisp. Add no features and move no UI.

RIGHT CANVAS CHANGE:
1. Remove the current tall visible colored sheet/arc along the right edge COMPLETELY. Remove its filled pastel area, glass surface volume, curved outline and diagonal silhouette. The top and side of the canvas return to the calm existing warm white/pale-gray dot-grid background.
2. In the LOWEST 20-25% of the right canvas, overlay a refined low-contrast ornamental web of continuous, very thin, soft curving paths. The paths softly sweep from lower right toward lower left; some converge, briefly weave, branch and continue, suggesting connections and shared flow. A sparse connective filigree, not a standalone illustration. No enclosed filled shapes, no large color patches, no solid ribbon or glass object.
3. Use subtle MULTI-HUE GRADIENTS ALONG THE FINE LINES: pale cyan/periwinkle, a little mint and muted rose/apricot. Approximate 5-9% visible strength on the near-white background. Keep only 4-6 main meandering trajectories and a few faint connecting echoes; plenty of calm whitespace. Add exquisite minute optical texture rather than dense visual noise. The implied connectivity comes from continuity and shared intersections.
4. Feather/fade the pattern upward and at all outside edges across wide smooth transitions. The pattern must feel softly printed INTO the canvas surface underneath the content. No clear bounding rectangle, hard outline, dark shadow, glowing rim, strong gradient blob or saturated band.
5. The pattern does not reserve a footer slot or shift objects. It can extend beneath existing cards, minimap and controls at the BACKGROUND layer, while those UI surfaces/text stay crisp, neutral and fully readable. It must not visually attach to cards or follow their outlines.

Avoid functional-diagram semantics: NO nodes, arrows, endpoint dots, numbers, labels, straight orthogonal circuits, iconography or connections to actual canvas cards. No chart, no fake card relationship, no clickable-looking marks. No spheres/pearls, physical hardware, extra panel, divider or artwork caption. Decoration is atmospheric continuity, not an operation.
Output one polished screen, with the left and middle unchanged and only the right-side solid decoration replaced by this faint bottom connective pattern.
